hook: These Special Oils Fight Fungus Resistance And Support Healthy Nails And Skin
claim: Kerassentials is a nail and skin oil applied daily after showering, sold for toenail fungus. It combines essential oils with carrier oils and vitamins.
ing_note: The website lists these oils and 'skin supporting vitamins' (the cited 2020 study used a vitamin E and essential-oil nail oil). Concentrations are not disclosed.
use: Apply to the affected nails and skin every day after showering.
price_note: Kerassentials is sold as 2 bottles (+$9.99 shipping), 2+1 bottles or 3+3 bottles with free shipping; totals appear on the order page.
checks: Unlike many competitors, Kerassentials cites relevant studies: a 2017 tea tree oil trial for onychomycosis and a 2020 open study of a vitamin E and essential-oil nail oil.
Those studies were small and short; tea tree oil cures only a minority of nails in trials.
The page correctly notes, citing the CDC, that people often stop antifungal treatment too early; nail fungus takes 6–12 months to grow out.
Bonus claims (such as dessert recipes that 'flush out hidden fungal cells') aren't evidence-based.
pros: Contains tea tree oil, the best-studied natural option
cons: Modest effectiveness even for tea tree oil
verdict: Kerassentials is one of the more reasonable nail-fungus products because tea tree oil has real, if modest, evidence. Expect slow results and keep using it for months. For thick or widespread fungus, prescription topical or oral antifungals have much higher cure rates, so it's worth seeing a doctor. Essential oils can irritate skin; stop if you get a rash.
